question.text: Konark Growth Fund (Cat II): Capital called INR 120 crore. Cumulative distributions to LPs (DPI cash out) = INR 144 crore. Residual NAV (unrealised) = INR 96 crore. Compute TVPI.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, TVPI = (cumulative distributions + residual value) / Paid-In Capital, and equivalently TVPI = DPI + RVPI. Here: (INR 144 + INR 96) / INR 120 = INR 240 / INR 120 = 2.00x. Cross-check: DPI = 144/120 = 1.20x; RVPI = 96/120 = 0.80x; DPI + RVPI = 2.00x. The Trap: Option A reports only DPI. Option C reports only RVPI. Option B (2.40x) divides the numerator by capital called minus residual or applies an incorrect base — it does not reconcile to DPI + RVPI. Note: Always confirm whether a question asks for DPI, RVPI, or TVPI before computing; these are distinct metrics with the same inputs.
